subject.title: Agent lane lacks first-class scoped node exec path and stale nodes can hang or fail roughly

question: Should OpenClaw support mixed local Codex native execution plus a separate first-class node exec dynamic tool or binding, and what security and stale-node contract should that surface expose?
rationale: The code change is not just a bug patch: it creates a new remote-shell surface inside agent lanes and must choose node selection, visibility, approval, audit, and retry semantics.

options.title: Add scoped mixed-session node exec
options.body: Expose a secondary `node_exec`-style binding for trusted sessions with host/node pinned by OpenClaw, existing approval/audit policy preserved, and stale nodes returned as structured retryable failures.

options.title: Keep node exec host-policy gated
options.body: Leave `node_exec` visible only when the effective session exec host is `node`, document that mixed local-default sessions need another workflow, and close or narrow this request.

options.title: Use capability-specific node tools
options.body: Avoid a generic shell surface in mixed sessions and prefer narrower node-hosted plugin or MCP tools for the workflows that need laptop access.

recommendation.title: Add scoped mixed-session node exec
recommendation.body: Expose a secondary `node_exec`-style binding for trusted sessions with host/node pinned by OpenClaw, existing approval/audit policy preserved, and stale nodes returned as structured retryable failures.

likelyOwner.reason: The open decision is centered on the Codex dynamic-tool surface introduced in PR #93654.
